baseline-first.note: Both sets capture the section designations and datum elevations, but Set A misbinds C3X6 to the West Building Elevation when it appears only in the North Elevation – Bedroom view, and adds an unsupported derived claim ("W10X | weight | 12 lb/ft") that the sheet never states. Set B keeps its condition bindings consistent with the view each label appears in (HSS4X4X1/4, HSS4X6X1/4, C8X11.5, L3x3x1/4 on East; W8X10, W10X12, HSS on West) and also captures the SOLAR ENVELOPE 18'-0" datum and T.O. STEEL 11'-4" for both elevations, which Set A omits. Set B's claims are all supported by quoted text, with only minor duplication and a debatable "Beam" role label for the C8X11.5 channel.

variant-first.note: A binds the datum labels to the right elevations (T.O. STEEL 11'-4" on both East and West, SOLAR ENVELOPE 18'-0" on the West elevation) and keeps more section/elevation pairings that the text supports (HSS4X6X1/4 and C8X11.5 on the East elevation, L3x3x1/4" and W8X10 on East/West). B drops the solar-envelope and West T.O. STEEL facts, mis-binds C3X6 to the West elevation when it appears only on the North/Bedroom elevation, and invents a "W10X | weight | 12 lb/ft" claim (with a garbled quote) out of the W10X12 designation. A's clear error is HSS4X6X1/4 listed for the West elevation, where only HSS4X4X1/4 appears, plus calling the C8X11.5 channel a "Beam"; B also has two mangled plate quotes and several vague "component" claims.

baseline-first.note: Both sets contain the same seven claims with identical values, bindings, and supporting quotes, all of which are faithful to the page text (47,402.91 N•m saturation, 15,000 N•m/s rate limit, 1173.7 rpm rated speed, high drivetrain damping, no torsional-vibration control loop, single-DOF = shaft angular rotation, and the blade-pitch control goal). The only difference is that Set A adds the condition 'Region 3' to the rated generator speed claim, which is a reasonable contextual qualifier since the value appears in the Region 3 pitch-control discussion, though rated speed is not strictly a Region-3-only property. Neither set invents values or misbinds attributes, and both omit the same minor facts (e.g., the 1° blade-pitch trigger and 10% above rated).

variant-first.note: Both sets contain the same seven claims with identical values, bindings, and quotes; the only difference is that B adds 'conditions: Region 3' to the rated generator speed claim. That condition is supported by the surrounding sentence (the PI control in Region 3 uses the rated generator speed), though rated speed is itself a general generator property, so the addition is neutral rather than an error. Neither set misreads, misbinds, or invents anything, and both capture the key torque saturation, rate limit, damping, and control-structure facts.

baseline-first.note: Both sets are essentially identical in content and share the same defects: the Living Room finished floor value 2' - 3 1/2" is not in the text layer (both sections read 2' - 9 1/2"), and 'Mechanical Room | location | Building Section A302' mislabels the sheet number A-302 as a building section. The only differences are naming precision on the scale claims: B binds the scales to 'Living Room Section (A1)' and 'Section - Centre Module (C1)', while A uses the looser 'Section C1' and 'Living Room Section'. Both also carry the same vague/duplicative claims (repeated finished-floor and grade-level elevations, 'building section | contains room', tautological 'WEST MODULE | location | West').

variant-first.note: The two sets are nearly identical in content: both capture the 3/8" = 1'-0" scales for sections A1 and C1, the 2' - 9 1/2" finished floor and 0' - 0" grade datum, and the room contents of the Living Room and Centre Module sections. Both contain the same misread claim of 2' - 3 1/2" for the Living Room finished floor (the text layer and image both read 2' - 9 1/2"), the same vague 'CENTRE MODULE location K' and 'WEST MODULE location West' claims, and the same mislabeled 'Building Section A302' (A-302 is the sheet number). The only differences are trivial rewordings and one duplicated A1 scale claim in each set, so neither is more faithful than the other.

baseline-first.note: Both sets read the wiring schedule rows correctly for the most part, but Set A binds more of the schedule's key details — ground conductor sizes for items 20, 50 and 34, conduit sizes for items 31, 34 and 50, and AL material for schedule 150 — which Set B omits. Set B does capture a few facts A misses (150's 2-1/2" conduit, 151's ARMORED CABLE type and 3#4/0 size, item 31's 2#10), but it twice stuffs the row's material 'CU' into a bogus conditions field and labels the attribute merely 'conductor', making those claims vague and mis-fielded. Set A's only real defect is one spurious condition 'C.' on item 34's conduit size, where 'C.' is just the abbreviation for conduit in the quote. Overall A is the more faithful and complete extraction.

Both sets share the same notable misbinding — 9'-0" is a horizontal dimension string, not the FIRST FLR / T.O. STEEL elevation relative to GRADE LEVEL (that datum is 2'-4" and 11'-4") — and both repeat several facts verbatim. Set A is more redundant (PL3"X1/4" and HSS4X4X1/4 each appear four times, plus duplicated 8" and 2'-4" claims), so much of its volume is trivial. Set B has fewer duplicates and additionally captures real page facts A misses (32'-0", 7 7/8", 3'-1", and the 11'-4" T.O. STEEL level), while A's unique items (10'-0", 3", 8", HSS4X6X1/4) are mostly generic or weakly bound. B's only soft spot is the vague 'unspecified structural element' entity and a generic drawing-scale claim.

variant-first.note: Both sets share the same core member sizes (HSS4X4X1/4, W6X20, W8X10, L3x3x1/4, PL3"X1/4) and both repeat the same misbound claim that 9'-0" is the FIRST FLR/T.O. STEEL elevation above GRADE LEVEL, when 9'-0" is a plan/width dimension and the datums read 2'-4" and 11'-4". Set A adds more distinct, supported facts that B omits: the T.O. STEEL 11'-4" elevation, the 32'-0" overall dimension, 3'-1", 7 7/8", and the 1/4"=1'-0" scale for the EAST elevation. Set B's extras are mostly redundant restatements of the plate/HSS labels plus 3", 10'-0" and 8", and it drops the 11'-4" datum entirely. A's only added weakness is one vague 'unspecified structural element' claim for 8'-8 1/2".

baseline-first.note: Both sets cover the same substantive facts from Rule 9-4 and the dinner-party guest count, with values correctly bound to the TV display, computer display, and dinner party, and quotes that support each claim. Set A adds two claims ('computer display minimum size 38.1 cm' and 'TV display minimum size 68.6 cm') that merely restate values already captured in both sets under the manufacturer-stated display size attribute, so they are redundant rather than new or wrong. Neither set misreads, misbinds, or invents anything, and both already express each size in both inches and centimeters, so the substantive content is equivalent.

variant-first.note: Both sets correctly capture the display size minimums (TV 27 in./68.6 cm, computer 15 in./38.1 cm), the 75% TV brightness requirement, the 8-person dinner minimum with its guest composition, and the simultaneous/independent operation requirement, with quotes that support each claim and nothing invented. The two sets cover exactly the same facts; Set B simply adds two further restatements of facts it already lists (computer 38.1 cm and TV 68.6 cm), increasing redundancy without adding information. Since both are equally accurate and neither omits an important fact, the only differentiator is that Set A carries fewer duplicate/trivial claims.

baseline-first.note: Both sets are accurate and faithful on the shared claims, with quotes correctly supporting the stated goals, configuration, filter type, and variable definitions. Set A adds three further supported claims that Set B omits: the full-span rotor-collective blade-pitch controller operating above rated wind speed in power-production operation, the generator-torque controller operating below rated wind speed in power-production operation, and the two power-production control systems of the NREL 5-MW baseline turbine. Set A's extras are somewhat redundant with its other claims but are not wrong, so its coverage of the page is more complete while neither set invents facts.

variant-first.note: Both sets are factually accurate against the page: goals of the torque and pitch controllers, the below-/above-rated ranges, the filter type and y/u definitions, the turbine configuration, and the absence of nonpower-production control actions are all correctly quoted and bound. Set B adds one valid binding (full-span rotor-collective blade-pitch controller in the above-rated range) but otherwise repeats facts already present, yielding three near-duplicate claims (the two control-systems claims, the two generator-torque range claims, and the two nonpower-production claims). Set A covers essentially the same content with only two duplicates, so it is the leaner, less redundant set; neither set invents values or misbinds properties, and both omit the nacelle-yaw and filter-coefficient details equally.

baseline-first.note: Both sets capture the same core facts — 1:1 depth-to-height ratio, the Height = D*1.2 simplification, 0° window azimuth, truncated isosceles triangle louver shape, powder-coated finish, 25° structural bend, and 50° solar altitude at fall equinox 12pm — with quotes that support them. Set A adds three redundant duplicates of claims already present (depth-to-height ratio, louver shape, 25° bend), making it more repetitive without adding information. Set B has one fewer duplicate but truncates a condition field ('along the louver longit'), a minor misread; net defects are essentially equal, and both omit the proportional spacing reduction based on average profile widths.

variant-first.note: Both sets cover the same core facts (50° solar altitude at fall equinox noon, 0° window azimuth, the Height = Depth*tan(solar elevation)/Cos(solar azimuth–window azimuth) and Height = D*1.2 formulas, 1:1 depth-to-height ratio, truncated isosceles triangle louver shape, 25° structural bend, powder-coated finish) with supporting quotes. Both contain redundant duplicate claims (shape, bend angle, and in B also the 1:1 ratio), but B additionally misbinds the 25° angle to the 'louver longitudinal section' as the entity rather than to the louver's bend, and repeats the ratio claim. A's only notable flaw is one bend claim with a truncated condition string ('along the louver longit'), so A is marginally cleaner and more faithful.

baseline-first.note: Both sets share most claims, including the dubious pairing of keynote code 05 12 23.A7 as a 'specification' of the HSS and the unsupported 'C3X6 quantity 1'. Set A adds two claims with fabricated or misbound quotes: 'W10X12 TYP' (the text has W10X12 and 1/4" TYP as separate annotations) and 'C3X6 length 1'-4"' (1'-4" is a standalone dimension, not a length of the channel). Set B instead correctly captures the HSS member size 4X4X1/4 from HSS4X4X1/4, which A omits, so B is the more faithful set despite its duplicate W8X10 entries and the shared 'TYP C3X6' invented quote.

variant-first.note: Both sets capture the section designations (C3X6, W8X10, W10X12, W10X15, L3x3x1/4, L4X4X5/16, PL5X3/8, PL 4 1/2X4 1/2X1/2) and the 1/4" TYP dimensions with supporting quotes. Set A additionally extracts the HSS 4X4X1/4 member size, which is clearly present in the text and reference keynotes. Set B adds a plausible 1'-4" length for C3X6 but misbinds the TYP condition to W10X12 (the TYP in the text applies to the 1/4" weld/plate dimensions, not the beam section) and includes a vague duplicate 'section profile' claim. Set A's only notable weakness is the 'C3X6 quantity 1' claim, where the '1' is likely a detail callout rather than a quantity (a claim also present in B).

baseline-first.note: Both sets capture the same core facts faithfully: window azimuth 0 for the southern louver, 50-degree solar altitude at fall equinox 12pm, the depth-to-height algorithm, the 25-degree structural bend, and the 1:1 depth-to-height ratio, all with supporting quotes. Set A adds an eighth claim that simply duplicates the truncated-isosceles-triangle shape claim without its 'extruded' condition, which is redundant and trivial rather than new information. Set B is therefore marginally cleaner, though both sets share the same weaknesses: truncated quotes ('windo', 'longit') and a vague 'solar altitude | value' claim with a non-component entity. No claims in either set are misread or invented.

variant-first.note: Both sets capture the same core facts correctly: window azimuth 0, 50-degree solar altitude at fall equinox 12pm, the depth-to-height algorithm, the 25-degree structural bend, and the 1:1 louver ratio, with quotes that support them. Set B adds a redundant duplicate of the truncated-isosceles-triangle shape claim without its 'extruded' condition, which is trivial clutter. Both sets also share a weakly bound claim where 'solar altitude' is used as the entity with attribute 'value', which is vague and misbound. Because B carries the extra redundant claim and nothing additional of value, A is marginally better.

baseline-first.note: Both sets capture the main spanwise trends (chord ~5.7 m near r/R=0.25, twist 15 deg at root and ~-2 deg near 0.85, prebend 0 to -4 m, pitch-axis location 50% to ~29% to 37%). Set A's extra errors are a conflicting chord value of 0.6 m at r/R=1.0 and a 20% relative thickness at r/R=1.0 alongside its correct 22% entry. Set B adds more conflicting/wrong readings: chord 1.5 m at r/R=1.0, pitch-axis 38% at r/R=1.0 contradicting its own 37%, and relative thickness 20% at r/R=0.0 contradicting the 100% root value shown in plot (b). Set A also redundantly repeats a few correct claims, but its wrong claims are fewer and less severe.

variant-first.note: Both sets read the same five spanwise curves and share several flaws: relative thickness 95% at r/R=0 (curve starts at 100%), twist -1.5 deg at r/R=1.0 (curve ends near -1 deg), a 22% thickness claim whose quote cites '20 ... 0.7', and duplicated twist -2 deg at 0.85. Set A adds extra errors: relative thickness 20% at r/R=0 (clearly wrong), a conflicting pitch-axis value of 38% at r/R=1.0 alongside 37%, and a conflicting chord of 1.5 m at r/R=1.0 alongside 0.5 m, plus a duplicate prebend -4 m claim. Set B's unique problems are milder: a duplicated chord 5.7 m at ~0.25 and pitch-axis 50% at 0.0, and a conflicting chord 0.6 m at r/R=1.0, while it correctly adds prebend 0 m at r/R=0 and thickness 20% at the tip. Overall B binds values to the right properties and stations with fewer outright misreads.

baseline-first.note: Both sets correctly capture the nine drivetrain properties from Table 5-1 with accurate values, units, and supporting quotes, including the fully-deployed condition on the brake torque. Set A, however, adds a redundant tenth claim (Rotor | Rated Speed | 12.1 rpm) that duplicates its own Rated Rotor Speed entry, adding no new information. Set B is otherwise identical in content and binding, so it is the cleaner, equally complete extraction.

variant-first.note: Both sets capture the nine drivetrain properties in Table 5-1 with correct values, units, and supporting quotes, including the fully-deployed condition on the brake torque. Set B adds a tenth claim (Rotor | Rated Speed | 12.1 rpm) that merely duplicates its own 'Rated Rotor Speed' claim, adding no new information and only redundancy. Otherwise the two sets are identical in accuracy and binding, so A is slightly better for its cleaner, non-redundant output.

baseline-first.note: Both sets bind values, conditions and quotes correctly against the page, with no invented or misread claims. Set A, however, contains four redundant near-duplicate claims (Lynx mirror assembly diameter, Origins telescope diameter, LUVOIR-A telescope diameter, LUVOIR-B telescope diameter) that restate facts already captured under slightly different entity labels. Set B covers the same complete set of facts (all diameters, focal length, instrument counts, starshade size) without this duplication, so it is the cleaner, equally faithful extraction.

variant-first.note: Both sets capture the same core facts accurately, with values, units, and quotes correctly bound to each mission concept. Set B, however, contains four redundant duplicate claims (Lynx mirror assembly diameter, Origins telescope diameter, and LUVOIR-A/LUVOIR-B telescope diameter restated under slightly different entity names), adding trivial noise without new information. Set A covers the identical complete set of facts with no duplicates or errors, making it the cleaner and more faithful extraction.

baseline-first.note: Both sets pad their output by misreading the legend callouts (circled 3 = Sunpreme GX290 module, circled 11 = #10G bonding jumper) as numeric 'values', 'quantities' or connection targets, but Set B does this more often and adds clear misbindings: it attributes the U.V. rating to the current-carrying cable (note 2 assigns it to cable ties), invents SA3-2/SA3-3 connections to the mounting rails, and calls the 11 callout an 'interconnecting component value'. Set A is more faithful on the notes and legend (USE-2 10 G.A. cable spec with its 'all current carrying cable' condition, frameless glass design) and keeps a consistent, supported series polarity pattern (- to +) across the strings, with only two invented polarities (SA2-25 to WEATHERHEAD, SA2-26 to SA2-27). Set B does capture two facts A misses (NEMA 3R junction box on side of house, SUNPREME GX290 model) plus the planter-equipment feed, but it carries more wrong and unsupported claims overall.

variant-first.note: Set A captures the page's key engineering facts that Set B omits: the NEMA 3R junction box on the side of the house, the Sunpreme GX290 module model, and the connection to planter equipment (see E-206), plus the USE-2 10 G.A cable note. Set B does get the frameless glass design and several series-connection polarities right, but it drops the junction-box rating and module model and states the SA2-26 to SA2-27 polarity as positive-to-positive, which contradicts the drawn terminal marks. Set A's clear defects are the U.V. rating misbound to the current-carrying cable (the note assigns it to cable ties) and two claims built on the '11' bonding-jumper symbol treated as a value or connection target. Both sets pad with trivial 'value 3' claims, but A's coverage of the substantive notes and labels is more complete.

baseline-first.note: Both sets share the same core claims (3/8" through bolt, Module A/B total lengths 12'-3 3/4" and 10'-3 3/4", L3X3X1/4 profiles, and the 5/16" bolt callout), and both carry the same vague 'PV Detail | dimension' entries. Set A additionally captures the L3X3X1/4 member profile shown in the Module B detail, which Set B omits. Set A's only defect is a redundant second 'Through Bolt | diameter | 3/8"' claim that misuses the S-301 reference tag as a condition. On balance A carries one more supported, correctly bound claim than B.

variant-first.note: Both sets capture the main dimensions, the L3X3X1/4 angle profiles, and the 3/8" through bolts, and both carry the same questionable claim of a 5/16" bolt (the text layer shows 5/8", not 5/16"). Set B additionally captures the L3X3X1/4 member profile shown in the Module B detail, which Set A omits. However, Set B adds a duplicate Through Bolt claim that misuses the S-301 reference keynote as a condition, and Set A's first quote is slightly contaminated by appending S-301. On balance B recovers one more supported fact while incurring one extra trivial/duplicated claim.

baseline-first.note: The two sets are nearly identical in content, values, units, and quotes, covering the same drivetrain properties from both the prose and Table 5-1. Both redundantly list the fully-deployed brake torque twice (once from prose, once from the table), and both keep the gearbox no-frictional-losses condition and the brake time-lag condition. The only differences are trivial wording variants (e.g., 'Rated Speed' vs 'Rated Rotor Speed' for the rotor, and whether 'fully-deployed' is carried in the attribute name or the conditions field), with no misread or invented values in either set. Both equally omit the driveshaft natural frequency and 5% critical damping ratio facts.

variant-first.note: The two sets are nearly identical in content, values, units, and quotes, both correctly capturing the drivetrain properties from the text and Table 5-1. The only differences are trivial: A labels the rotor claim 'Rated Rotor Speed' and adds an explicit 'fully-deployed' condition to the brake torque claim, while B encodes that condition in the attribute name. Both sets contain the same minor redundancy (brake torque stated twice) and both omit nothing important, so neither is meaningfully better.

baseline-first.note: Both sets contain the same four claims with identical values, conditions, and quotes; the only difference is that Set A expands the entity name 'TGen' to 'generator torque (TGen)'. Both correctly capture the Region 3 inverse-proportionality of generator torque, Eq. (7-6) and Eq. (7-7) formulas with their stated assumptions, and the PID blade-pitch law (7-10). Neither set invents facts or misbinds values, and both omit the same minor detail (the derivative term's ΔΩ̇ dot notation).

variant-first.note: Both sets contain the same four claims with identical values, conditions, and quotes, so their substantive content is equivalent. Both correctly capture the Region 3 inverse-proportional generator-torque relation, Eq. (7-6) and Eq. (7-7) formulas with their assumptions, but both misstate the PID law (Eq. 7-10) by dropping the derivative term's dot, writing K_D N_Gear ΔΩ instead of K_D N_Gear ΔΩ̇. The only difference is cosmetic: B names the entity 'generator torque (TGen)' where A writes just 'TGen'.

Both sets are largely accurate and share 20 of 25 claims, correctly binding conductor material, sizes, ground conductors and conduit sizes to the right schedule symbols (e.g. 20 = CU 3#12, #12G., 3/4"C.; 150 = AL 3#4/0, #4G., 2-1/2"C.). Set A adds clean, supported facts (34 conductor count/size 6#10, 50 conductor configuration 3#6, 150 conductor 3#4/0) with no errors, while Set B adds equally valid facts (151 conductor 3#4/0, 33 and 31 ground #10G, 150 conduit 2-1/2") but attaches an invented condition 'C.' to the 34 conduit-size claim, where 'C.' is only the abbreviation for conduit. Coverage of unique facts is about even, so the deciding defect is B's spurious condition field; A is marginally cleaner.

baseline-first.note: Both sets are drawn from the same wiring schedule rows (10, 20, 31–34, 50, 150, 151) and every claim in each is correctly bound to its row, with quotes that support the stated value. The two sets share 21 of 25 claims; Set A uniquely captures the 150 conduit size (2-1/2"C.) and ground-conductor sizes for items 31 and 33, while Set B uniquely captures conductor specs for 34, 50 and 150 plus the 32 conductor material. Neither set contains a misread, misbound or invented value, and each omits a comparable handful of schedule facts (A misses 34/50/150 conductor specs; B misses 150 conduit and the 31/33 grounds), so their overall accuracy and coverage are essentially equivalent.

Both sets bind the ø 3" opening diameter, W10X15 floor beam sections, W8X13 roof beam section, detail identifiers A1 and C1, and the 1/2" opening edge radius correctly with supporting quotes. Set A additionally captures the W10X15 section for Floor Beam @ Grid 5 (detail D5), which is supported by the sheet text and image. Set B omits this claim but introduces no errors, so A is the more complete set.

variant-first.note: Both sets capture the same core facts — the ø 3" beam openings, the 1/2" edge radius note, the W10X15 sections for the grid 2/3/4/near-5 beams, the W8X13 roof beam at grids 2–5, and the A1/C1 detail identifiers — with quotes that match the page text. Set B additionally includes the Floor Beam @ Grid 5 (detail D5) section W10X15, which is supported by the page and is an important fact that Set A omits. Neither set invents values or misbinds components, though both carry the 'T.O. STEEL' phrase from the E6 detail title as a condition, which is at worst a minor quibble shared equally. On balance Set B is the more complete extraction.

baseline-first.note: Both sets capture the core elevations, identifiers and cladding/handrail specs, and both repeat the same unsupported claim that the PV array sits between grid lines 4 and 6 plus an invented 'roof/overhang' binding. Set B adds several correct, distinct facts Set A misses (APSE-20 tube model, powdercoated steel flatbar railing posts, West Elevation scale 1/4"=1'-0", the note that tube-array spacing may be larger, and identifiers W1 1.01 and W2 1.04). Set A does capture facts B omits (40 tubes, 1/8" cable diameter, A-511 Hardie reference, W5 1.14), but it pads the set with near-duplicate claims and a trivial 'PV SOLAR ARRAY presence: installed' claim whose quote does not support it. Net, B is slightly more faithful and less redundant.

variant-first.note: Both sets capture the window/door identifiers, elevations and railing/cladding materials correctly, but Set A binds the datum labels more faithfully (elevation 18'-0", 2'-9 1/2", 0'-0") and preserves the note-2 condition that tube-array spacing may be larger, plus the APSE-20 model and the 1/4"=1'-0" scale. Set B adds two good facts A misses (40 tubes total, A-511 Hardie reference, 1/8" cable diameter) but mislabels elevations as 'height'/'dimension', includes a trivial 'PV SOLAR ARRAY presence: installed' claim and several duplicates. Both share the vague 'roof/overhang = PV SOLAR ARRAY' claim; on balance A has fewer misbound or trivial claims.

baseline-first.note: Both sets capture the same core details (14/16 gauge plates, #10 TEK screws, HSS4X4X1/4, W6X20, 28" footing, 6" min/max opening dims) and share the same flaws: the bolt quote fabricates a '3"' that appears only as a separate dimension, the (4) 3/4" holes are bound to a deck opening plate although they sit in the foundation detail, and 1'-0" is labeled MIN in the text layer but reported as the opening's maximum. B additionally binds the 3" std pipe and PL5x4x3/8 to the PV attachment detail (A1), where they actually appear, whereas A leaves them as vague generic 'pipe' and 'plate' claims that collide with its separate PL5X3/8 plate claim. B is therefore slightly more faithful in component binding with no additional errors.

variant-first.note: The two sets are nearly identical in content and share the same defects: both insert an unsupported "3"" into the bolt quote/condition (the text reads "3/4" BOLT NUT WELDED TO WIDE FLANGE" with 3" as a separate dimension), both misbind the (4) 3/4" DIA HOLES to a deck opening plate when they belong to the foundation detail, and both use stitched quotes ("3/8" FITTED STIFFENER", "16 GAUGE PLATE OF OPENING"). The only differences favor A: it correctly binds PL5x4x3/8 and the 3" std. pipe to the PV attachment detail ("PV attachment plate", "PV attachment pipe"), whereas B leaves them as vague generic "plate" and "pipe". A is therefore marginally more faithful and specific.

baseline-first.note: Both sets capture the two substantive facts on the page: the near-linear variation of pitch sensitivity with blade-pitch angle in Region 3, and the rated mechanical power of 5.296610 MW, each with supporting quotes. Set A adds a third claim that merely duplicates its rated-power claim (same value and quote, only dropping the 'rated' condition), which is redundant and trivial rather than additional evidence. Set B therefore delivers the same correct content with no filler, while neither set misreads or invents values. Missing table data (e.g., ∂P/∂θ values) is absent from both, so it does not differentiate them.

variant-first.note: Both sets correctly capture the near-linear dependence of pitch sensitivity on blade-pitch angle in Region 3 and the rated mechanical power of 5.296610 MW with supporting quotes. Set B adds a third claim that merely duplicates its rated-power claim while dropping the 'rated' condition, which is a trivial, redundant entry rather than new information. Set A is therefore the cleaner, equally faithful set; the turbine entity name is not stated on this page but is used identically by both, so it does not differentiate them.

baseline-first.note: Both sets cover the four Table 6-2 properties and both contain redundant duplicate claims (A has three duplicate pairs, B two). Set A preserves the important damping condition — 1% critical in all modes of the isolated tower without the rotor-nacelle assembly mass — while Set B drops the isolated-tower/RNA-mass condition, leaving the damping claim incomplete. Otherwise the values, units and quotes are correctly bound in both, so A is slightly better for keeping the needed condition.

variant-first.note: Both sets correctly capture the four Table 6-2 tower properties with supporting quotes, and both contain redundant duplicate claims (A repeats the CM location; B repeats the mass and CM location). Set B is stronger on the damping claim because it retains the stated condition 'isolated tower (without rotor-nacelle assembly mass present)', which Set A drops, keeping only 'all modes'. Set B's minor blemishes are the vague 'conditions: overall' on height and the duplicated mass/CM entries, but no values are misbound or invented in either set. Overall B preserves the needed conditions better at the cost of a couple of trivial duplicates.

Both sets capture the same core facts: the 40W/9W/7W light-output equivalence example, the T24 high-efficacy requirement for HARVEST HOME fixtures, and the vacancy-sensor dimming-bypass requirement with its condition. Both contain near-duplicate claims (the 40W incandescent and the vacancy-sensor requirement each appear twice), and B adds a third redundancy by listing the HARVEST HOME requirement twice, once without the Title 24 condition. Neither set extracts the LIGHTING LEVELS table (foot-candle levels and bulb counts per activity), so both are equally incomplete there. Set A is marginally better only because it carries one fewer redundant claim.

baseline-first.note: Both sets correctly capture the 40W/9W/7W light-output equivalence, the T24 high-efficacy requirement for HARVEST HOME fixtures, and the vacancy-sensor dimming-bypass requirement with proper conditions and supporting quotes. Set A adds one extra claim that is merely a duplicate of its own T24 requirement claim (without conditions), making it more redundant than Set B. Neither set is factually wrong, but both duplicate the incandescent 40W and vacancy-sensor claims and both omit the page's lighting-levels table (3/5-10/30/50 FC) and the own-switch requirement for kitchen, bathroom, closet and laundry rooms. Because Set B carries fewer trivial duplicate claims while keeping the same correct content, it is slightly better.

variant-first.note: Both sets bind the beam sections correctly to their detail callouts (D5, C1, A4, A1, B4, B1, C4, E6) with supporting quotes, and neither invents values.
